title: Standardize retry/backoff behavior + Retry-After handling (SDK parity v1)
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Python SDK now uses standardized retry defaults (429/5xx + network errors) with exponential backoff + jitter and respects Retry-After when present. New knobs: max_retries/max_attempts, backoff tuning, and a switch to disable Retry-After honoring. No API surface redesign; behavioral change is limited to defaults and is configurable.
body: Summary: Implements the cross-language retry policy standard for the Python SDK: retry on 429 + transient 5xx + selected network/transport errors, exponential backoff with jitter, and proper Retry-After parsing (seconds and HTTP-date formats). Exposes configuration knobs on the client so customers can tune or disable behavior. Context: This is part of the SDK parity initiative (ENG-5120) to eliminate "works in TS but not in Python" inconsistencies, reduce support cases around intermittent 429/5xx/timeouts, and align SDK behavior with platform signals (Retry-After, request_id). Behavior (defaults): max_attempts=4 total (1 initial + up to 3 retries); retryable HTTP status codes: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 (and 408 when the server responds with it); non-retryable: all other 4xx (e.g., 400/401/403/404/409/422) to avoid duplicate side-effects and billing confusion; retryable network errors: connect errors, DNS resolution errors, connection resets, TLS handshake errors, and read timeouts raised by the underlying HTTP client; backoff: exponential starting at 0.5s, capped at 8s, using jitter (full jitter by default) to reduce herd behavior; Retry-After: if present on a retryable response (notably 429), we honor it as the minimum delay, clamped to max_backoff to avoid extremely long sleeps in client code. Retry-After parsing details: supports integer seconds ("Retry-After: 5") and HTTP-date (RFC 7231 style). If the date is in the past or unparseable, we fall back to computed backoff. Config surface (new/standardized): ClientOptions: max_attempts (int), max_retries (int alias; deprecated warning if both set and disagree), initial_backoff (seconds), max_backoff (seconds), jitter ("full" | "none"), retry_on_status (list override), respect_retry_after (bool, default true). Request-level override: per-request options allow disabling retries (retries=0) for non-idempotent calls or workflows where the caller already handles retries. Notes on streaming: this PR does NOT add automatic retries for streaming responses. Streaming retries remain opt-in and should be implemented at the application layer with idempotency guidance (tracked separately); the retry middleware explicitly bypasses streaming iterators to avoid duplicating partial outputs. Implementation overview: Added a RetryPolicy abstraction used by both sync and async clients; implemented RetryAfterParser that accepts seconds or HTTP-date and returns a delay; integrated policy into the HTTP transport wrapper to centralize decision logic (status/network classification, sleep, attempt counting); ensured we propagate request_id into raised errors (when present) so callers can correlate retries with server logs; added unit tests using mocked responses and transport exceptions; updated docstrings and examples for configuration knobs and safe defaults. Files/areas changed (high level): redwood/_http/retry.py (new RetryPolicy + backoff), redwood/_http/transport.py (wiring), redwood/_client.py (options plumbed), redwood/errors.py (ensure request_id survives wrapping), tests/test_retry_policy.py, tests/test_retry_after.py, tests/test_transport_retries.py, docsstrings in client options and README snippets. Illustrative snippet (Python): options = RedwoodOptions(api_key=..., max_attempts=6, initial_backoff=0.25, max_backoff=10.0, respect_retry_after=True); client = Redwood(options=options) // client.chat.completions.create(...). Alternatively per-request: client.chat.completions.create(..., request_options={"max_attempts": 1}) to disable retries. Why these defaults: SRE guidance was to avoid retry storms under elevated 429s; honoring Retry-After and adding jitter is critical for protecting the gateway and improving tail latency. We intentionally do not retry 400-series validation errors to avoid duplicate actions and billing disputes (see SUP-29438). Testing: Unit tests cover: 429 with Retry-After seconds; 429 with Retry-After HTTP-date; malformed Retry-After; Retry-After in the past; 500/502/503/504 backoff increments and jitter; non-retryable 400 does not retry; transport exceptions (connect/reset/read timeout) retry; max_attempts respected; sleep is not invoked when retries disabled; streaming path bypasses retry wrapper. Rollout/compat: This changes default behavior for some callers who previously observed fewer retries (or immediate retries). Knobs are exposed; we also log a warning if legacy option names are used. Docs/migration notes will be updated in a separate docs PR for the cross-language parity release. Review notes: Ibrahim requested we clamp Retry-After to max_backoff (done) and ensure HTTP-date parsing uses timezone-aware values (done). Allison requested full-jitter by default and to document attempt counts (done). Marcus requested that we never log api_key values and that error messages mention configuration without printing secrets (no secrets logged; confirmed). Review conversation (highlights): Monica Patel: "Can we ensure Retry-After date parsing handles proxies that send RFC1123 with GMT?" Sabrina: "Yes, using email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime + UTC normalization; added tests." Ibrahim Khan: "Please avoid retrying 409s; TS had a bug retrying 400/409 and it caused duplicate side-effect concerns." Sabrina: "Confirmed: only 408/429 and 5xx per standard; added explicit test for 409." Allison Grant: "Default max_attempts=4 (3 retries) seems right; add jitter to reduce synchronization." Sabrina: "Implemented full-jitter; added note in docstring." CI: Initial run failed on lint (unused import in retry.py) and a flaky timing assertion in one test; fixed by mocking sleep and asserting call count/delays deterministically. Final checks: python-unit-tests (pass), lint (pass), typecheck (pass), packaging (pass). Merge: Squash merged into main; follow-up tickets: add conformance fixtures runner integration (ENG-5127) and update docs/migration notes (ENG-5128).
commits: sdk/python: add RetryPolicy + BackoffStrategy w/ jitter
sdk/python: parse and honor Retry-After (seconds + HTTP-date)
sdk/python: wire retry policy into sync + async transports
tests: add retry policy coverage for status codes + transport errors
requested_changes: Clamp Retry-After-derived delay to max_backoff; handle past-date headers; add explicit non-retry tests for 409/400; avoid sleeping in tests (mock sleep).
